title: Subsequent Keyboards Shortcuts require release/repress of modifier keys

actions.label: Add AltGr sequence to modifier tracking

comment.body: Thanks for confirming this on 0.102.2933. This should stay linked to #31571, with your exact regression sequence preserved: hold AltGr, press K then L without releasing it, and compare with releasing/repressing AltGr between the letters. The second mapping being missed is more specific than a generic shortcut failure. The tracker is not a shipped fix, and this does not justify changing Windows Sticky Keys settings or resetting your mappings.

judgment.recommended_action: Link31571 with this explicit AltGr sequence and current-version confirmation; avoid a competing speculative modifier patch.
evidence: The report maps leftCtrl+rightAlt+K/L to braces and distinguishes holding AltGr across both letters from releasing and pressing it again.
The latest affected-reporter reply confirms recurrence on0.102.2933; this is not a resolved old-version report.

Open31571 tracks Ctrl/Alt/Win sticky-state/remapping failures and is cross-referenced by this issue. Its scope matches the held-modifier state class, but no exact root cause or merged repair is identified here.
judgment.rationale: Preserve the unusually discriminating sequence as a regression case in the existing tracking work. The bot duplicate suggestion is corroborated by the actual behavior and tracker scope, not accepted on its own. Do not tell the reporter to turn on Sticky Keys or change every mapping.

fix_assessment.rationale: Existing open31571 provides modifier-state investigation coverage, not a proven fix for this exact AltGr sequence.
